nit: patch link or a gerrit topic would be nice to understand which patch your are referring to. I guess it is this one

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/91561
Thanks for the note. I will include the direct patch link to the dbus-sensors change in the updated commit message for Patch Set 3.

Sorry. you are completely right; I misunderstood the behavior here—Entity-Manager does not selectively drop individual properties during file loading. I will remove this confusing statement from the commit message.
could you add both of these to `required` array, otherwise it will be out of spec with D-Bus (D-Bus does not have optional properties).
Understood. I will add both OffsetValue and ScaleValue to the required array for TempSensor in legacy.json to remain compliant with the D-Bus specification.

Adding these to the required array in legacy.json will enforce these fields globally on all existing platform JSON configurations, causing massive validation failures across upstream platforms that do not use calibration.

I previously tried to add these two items, but it caused the OpenBMC CI build to fail. Is it possible to keep them optional in the EM schema? If I misunderstood your meaning, please correct me.

> Adding these to the required array in legacy.json will enforce these 
fields globally on all existing platform JSON configurations, causing 
massive validation failures across upstream platforms that do not use 
calibration.

would `"Offset": 0` and `"ScaleValue": 1.0` be sane defaults to set for those configs?

> Is it possible to keep them optional in the EM schema?

Yes, but EM should still expose them on D-Bus. That would require code changes in EM such that it exposes some default value in case the property is not configured.

Alternatively you could also add the properties as required in config. That would introduce some amount of bloat to existing configs, but it would be explicit and not break spec.

If you make the property as optional in EM config schema without changing code, it will break PDI/sdbusplus generated clients and those clients will not be able to use the interface. That's probably already the case but we don't have to make the problem worse.

I have implemented the latest patch set: the schema properties remain optional to prevent massive validation failures across existing upstream configs, but the Entity-Manager now dynamically populates `OffsetValue: 0.0` and `ScaleValue: 1.0` as fallback defaults on D-Bus when omitted from the JSON.

Sorry, my previous change with `itemType == "TempSensor"` didn't actually cover all devices under TempSensor in legacy.json. Please ignore the previous resolution, this is still unresolved. I will upload a proper fix.

To prevent breaking backward compatibility and causing validation failures across existing platform configurations, I have kept both `OffsetValue` and `ScaleValue` as optional fields in `legacy.json`.

Instead of making them required in the schema, I updated the `dbus_interface.cpp` to dynamically parse `legacy.json` at runtime, extract all valid `TempSensor` types from the schema's enum list, and inject sane defaults (`0.0` for offset, `1.0` for scale) onto D-Bus if they are omitted from the platform's system JSON.

I specifically wanted to avoid hardcoding or manually maintaining a static list of temperature sensor types in the code. By loading and parsing the schema dynamically, the implementation remains completely data-driven and automatically supports any future temperature devices added to the schema without requiring further code modifications.

This ensures PDI/sdbusplus generated clients can always safely consume these properties without bloating or breaking existing platform configs. Please let me know if this approach is acceptable to you.

> This ensures PDI/sdbusplus generated clients can always safely consume these properties without bloating or breaking existing platform
 configs. Please let me know if this approach is acceptable to you.

Thank you Peter, i really like your solution.

It might look like a special case now
(because we are adding it for tempsensor use case)

but it will easily extend to other configuration schemas in the future 😊

Thanks to your solution, when we add optional properties to the schemas in the future, we can simply extend the code you provided and add fallback defaults, ensuring compatibility with D-Bus spec and PDI generated clients, while keeping the handwritten configuration compact and the schemas backwards compatible.
I have uploaded a new patch set to follow all the comments.
Updated in the latest patch set. Thanks!

Doesn't the dbus sensors reactor already have to handle these not being present anyway?   Some systems have tons of temp sensors, I'm not necessarily a fan of adding default properties to D-Bus for each one that we know aren't even used, because if they were it would be in the JSON.

> Doesn't the dbus sensors reactor already have to handle these not being present anyway?

Yes, the linked patch treats these as optional. If EM provides default values, that is not necessary and no need to check for missing property.

> Some systems have tons of temp sensors, I'm not necessarily a fan of 
adding default properties to D-Bus for each one that we know aren't even
 used, because if they were it would be in the JSON.

Has the overhead of passing configuration via D-Bus ever been a bottleneck from your experience ? I have never benchmarked that so it would be interesting to know if that has been a problem for larger systems.

What is the tradeoff of having a few extra bytes passed via D-Bus versus
not being able to test the configuration parsing code on the reactor side because there is no machine readable interface definition -> no generated server.

What makes these properties different than all the other optional properties in the schema?

> no machine readable interface definition -> no generated server.

I'm not sure how that's relevant for hwmontempsensor that wouldn't use them anyway event after this change.

> What makes these properties different than all the other optional properties in the schema?

no particular difference

> I'm not sure how that's relevant for hwmontempsensor that wouldn't use them anyway event after this change.

fallback default values could grow into a generic EM feature starting with this patch, which would allow applying it to other schemas as well.

It's not that unreasonable to allow for default values in a configuration solution.

It simplifies the reactor code and moves us closer in terms of compatibility with D-Bus and generated codes.

If dbus-sensors doesn't want to unit test their configuration code path then that's their choice and they can continue to rely on the manual testing someone did 3 revisions ago that passed with their specific EM config.

For me the main points are

- internal compatibility with structured interface definitions
  and generated codes
- documenting the actual property type through the fallback default value (useful for writing clients)
- enabling better testing for reactors (via generated codes)

and i have been looking at this more from overall feature perspective rather than in context of a specific schema or reactor.

I can understand if you don't want this feature now because of lack of test coverage of the code being modified,

but i find the feature conceptually to probably be quite useful long term as it removes one concern (default values) from *N* reactor implementations into one place (EM)

So i will stick with my opinion but i am ok to revisit this later if it's too much features for code that doesn't have test coverage.
